items.title: K2-Horizon ships six fully open language models
items.summary: K2-Horizon is a fleet of six fully open language models, from a 0.9B dense model to a 375B-A23B MoE, built for general-purpose reasoning and agentic work. The release includes Mixture-of-Value Attention (MoVA), softplus attention gating, Uno diffusion adapters that speed up decoding by up to 2.2x, and the full development history, data, and code needed for transparency and reproducibility.

a i / k 2 / View arXiv page View PDF Project page Add to collection Community ztwang Paper author Paper submitter about 22 hours ago We present K2-Horizon, a fleet of six fully open language models, from a 0.9B dense model to a 375B-A23B MoE, built for general-purpose reasoning and agentic work acro
ss math and science, software engineering, deep research, office automation, and beyond.
The models lead or are competitive with strong open models of their size on agentic and coding benchmarks.

On the modeling side, to strengthen reasoning, we introduce Mixture-of-Value Attention (MoVA), applying MoE to attention value projections, and softplus attention gating, a more flexible, theoretically motivated gate.
Our 36B-A4B model uses both and nearly matches a 32B dense model trained on the same data, with one-seventh the active parameters.
We also introduce Uno, lossless diffusion adapters that speed up decoding by up to 2.2× without a separate draft model.

Our release follows the LLM360 definition of open source for transparency and reproducibility: the full development history, including intermediate checkpoints from every training stage, pre-training data, training logs, and all training, evaluation, and infrastructure code, notably our production-s
cale xLLM framework for dense and MoE training and the RL360 reinforcement-learning stack.
Beyond the data itself, we release and document in detail every pipeline that built it, the part of model development that open releases most rarely disclose.
These pipelines produced roughly 10T synthetic pre-training tokens, showing that synthetic data can be a major ingredient of pre-training at scale.
Four of the models share one 22T-token pre-training corpus and recipe, revealing consistent scaling behavior and enabling controlled studies of scale and sparsity.

items.title: Google rolls out Tasks in Gemini for free in six countries
items.summary: Google is updating Gemini to handle complex tasks like scheduling appointments, managing bills, and shopping for groceries, rolling this out free of charge across the U.S., Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia, and India using the Gemini 4 Hydrogen model. Gemini connects with more than 60 popular apps, and developers can apply to join the Connected Apps Platform.

evidence.quote: We’re updating Gemini to handle complex tasks like scheduling appointments, managing bills, and shopping for groceries.
By connecting to your emails, calendar, and payment methods, Gemini saves you time while keeping your data secure in isolated environments.
You can try these new capabilities today by switching the toggle from Chat to Task in the Gemini app, texting us on Android or iOS, or forwarding emails to gemini@google.com.
Starting now, this update is rolling out free of charge for hundreds of millions of people across the U.S., Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia, and India, using our new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model.
We’re also rolling out a set of advanced features, starting in the U.S.
I gave Gemini permission to access our utility portal with the new Google Password Manager integration and asked for it to analyze our past billing statements in my email.
Gemini quickly compared chargers thanks to Google’s Shopping Graph, asked me follow-up questions about the wattage and color, and then helped me check out using the new Google Pay integration.
Gemini now uses the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) to make purchases like this.
We’re working with American Express (coming soon), Mastercard, and Visa to keep your purchases secure with digital tokens on supported cards.

: “Add lasagna, strawberries, cucumbers, and vanilla ice cream to our Instacart order.” On the walk out, I saw an empty Cheerios box in the pantry, so I snapped a photo and sent a quick follow-up: “Add this too.” Gemini added it, and then handed me off to Instacart to complete the order.
Today, Gemini connects with more than 60 popular apps and, as a developer, you can apply to join our Connected Apps Platform .
When you assign Gemini a task, it uses Google Cloud’s Agent Compute Engine to work in a hardware-isolated virtual machine that’s dedicated to your account and never shared with other users.
Each virtual machine is sandboxed, so Gemini works in a separate, isolated environment that’s regularly tested by our security red teams.
For example, Gemini is designed to ask for your confirmation or pre-approval before clicking "Buy," and will ask clarifying questions if an instruction is ambiguous.

items.title: Meta brings the Muse personal AI agent to Australia
items.summary: Muse is a personal AI agent that takes tasks and projects off users' plate and turns long-term goals into action plans, and it is now available in Australia on iOS, Android, and muse.ai. Local connector partners include Canva, Domain, Kogan, MECCA, Officeworks, realestate.com.au, SWEAT, ShopBack, and Ticketek, with features rolling out progressively.

evidence.quote: Muse is a personal AI agent.
It doesn’t just answer questions, it actually does the work.
It helps people stay on top of things, takes tasks and projects off their plate, and turns long-term goals into action plans.
Muse is available in Australia from today, with local connector experiences across creativity, shopping, property, fitness and entertainment rolling out progressively.
Connectors are a big reason Muse can do so much.

People in Australia can connect their Muse to apps and services they already use, such as Gmail, Google Calendar, Instagram and OpenTable, so it can help them manage emails, coordinate schedules, draw on saved content and make a restaurant reservation—all part of getting everyday tasks done.
Early local connector partners in Australia include Canva, Domain, Kogan, MECCA, Officeworks, realestate.com.au, SWEAT, ShopBack, and Ticketek.
Connector features will roll out progressively, with some experiences becoming available after launch.
Canva, the global all-in-one visual communication platform that empowers anyone to design, is also available as a connector for Muse users around the world.
Real time conversations with your Muse are now possible on mobile, web or Mac.
Spaces , a custom experience you create inside Muse by describing your idea, is now also available.
Spaces can help you get things done, have a little fun, or give your creative projects a home, whether it’s a shopping hub, school dashboard, wedding planner, or trip planner to name a few ideas.

Muse runs on Muse Secure VM , a dedicated computer in the cloud that securely stores the data and credentials for the services you connect, while keeping passwords and payment methods out of the agent’s view.
You choose what your Muse can access, and it checks with you before sensitive actions such as sending an email or making a purchase.
Muse is available in Australia on iOS, Android, and muse.ai , a Mac app, and coming soon to AI glasses.

items.title: Maxwell-V1-Flash pairs MoE sparsity with 256K context
items.summary: Maxwell-V1.0-Flash is a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model developed by the Maxwell Team, with 35B total parameters, 3B active parameters per token, and support for context lengths up to 256K tokens. Its Maxwell Block Sparse Attention (MBSA) kernel is 6.7x faster than dense GQA at 256K, and the model ships with a vLLM OpenAI-compatible server image under the Apache License 2.0.

items.title: MiniMind trains a 64M-parameter LLM from scratch in 2h
items.summary: MiniMind is an open-source project that trains a roughly 64M-parameter ultra-small language model from scratch with about 3 yuan of cost and 2 hours of training time, reproducible on a single 3090. It covers the full training chain including MoE, Pretrain, SFT, LoRA, RLHF (DPO), RLAIF (PPO / GRPO / CISPO), Tool Use, Agentic RL, adaptive thinking, and distillation, with core algorithms implemented natively in PyTorch.

evidence.quote: 此开源项目旨在完全从 0 开始，仅用 3 块钱成本与 2 小时训练时间，即可训练出规模约为 64M 的超小语言模型 MiniMind。
MiniMind 系列极其轻量，主线最小版本体积约为 GPT-3 的 $\frac{1}{2700}$ ，力求让普通个人 GPU 也能快速完成训练与复现。
项目同时开源了大模型的极简结构与完整训练链路，覆盖 MoE、数据清洗、预训练（Pretrain）、监督微调（SFT）、LoRA、RLHF（DPO）、RLAIF（PPO / GRPO / CISPO）、Tool Use、Agentic RL、自适应思考与模型蒸馏等全过程代码。
MiniMind 同时拓展了视觉模态模型 MiniMind-V 、多模态 Omni 模型 MiniMind-O 、扩散语言模型（MiniMind-dLM）、线性模型（MiniMind-Linear），详见 Discussion 。
项目所有核心算法代码均从 0 使用 PyTorch 原生实现，不依赖第三方库提供的高层抽象接口。
提供完整的 MiniMind-LLM 结构代码（Dense + MoE），当前主线结构对齐 Qwen3 / Qwen3-MoE 生态。
覆盖 Pretrain、SFT、LoRA、RLHF-DPO、RLAIF（PPO / GRPO / CISPO）、Tool Use、Agentic RL、自适应思考与模型蒸馏等完整训练流程。
发布 minimind-3 / minimind-3-moe ：结构、Tokenizer、训练链路、推理接口与默认配置全面更新
结构主线对齐 Qwen3 / Qwen3-MoE 生态：Dense 约 64M ，MoE 约 198M-A64M ，并移除了 shared expert 设计
默认训练数据切换为 pretrain_t2t(_mini).jsonl 、 sft_t2t(_mini).jsonl 、 rlaif.jsonl 、 agent_rl.jsonl 与 agent_rl_math.jsonl
新增原生 Agentic RL 训练脚本 train_agent.py ，支持多轮 Tool-Use 场景下的 GRPO / CISPO
🔥支持llama.cpp、vllm、ollama等热门三方生态。
精简预训练数据集，并大幅提升预训练数据质量，大幅缩短个人快速训练所需时间，单卡3090即可2小时复现！
更新：LoRA微调脱离peft包装，从0实现LoRA过程；DPO算法从0使用PyTorch原生实现；模型白盒蒸馏原生实现。

items.title: SWE-CoWork benchmarks coding agents as digital employees
items.summary: SWE-CoWork is a benchmark of 101 development assignments across 101 real repositories, 11 programming languages, and 12 application domains, where agents work in a simulated engineering organization with 26 colleagues. The two leading models satisfy approximately 63% of fail-to-pass (F2P) tests but complete fewer than 8% of assignments, showing that partial implementation and complete task delivery remain far apart.

evidence.quote: We introduce SWE-CoWork, a benchmark comprising 101 development assignments across 101 real repositories, 11 programming languages, and 12 application domains.
Each assignment places an agent in a simulated engineering organization with 26 colleagues who have distinct responsibilities, bounded knowledge, and controlled collaboration behavior.

Starting from a brief handoff, agents must recover requirements distributed across colleagues and workplace records, reconcile conflicting evidence, and implement changes evaluated by private executable tests.
We evaluate eleven models and find a substantial gap between partial implementation and complete task delivery.
The two leading models satisfy approximately 63% of fail-to-pass (F2P) tests but complete fewer than 8% of assignments.
Providing complete requirements upfront improves F2P by approximately 16 percentage points for Seed Evolving and GPT-6 Astra, yet leaves complete task success unchanged.

Requirement-level trajectory analysis reveals failures throughout the delivery process: Claude-Opus-5.5 directs a mean of 93% of first questions about queried cards to their accountable owners across runs but obtains only 64% of colleague-held requirements.
Deferred questions go unfollowed, implementations remain incomplete even after requirements are acquired, and 31% of requirements reported as completed fail their tests.
These findings highlight sustained requirement tracking , from clarification through implementation, verification, and handoff, as a key challenge for reliable autonomous software engineering .

items.title: SPILLWAY separates target admission from sanitization for agents
items.summary: SPILLWAY defends tool-using agents against prompt injection by checking whether a call's target value came from a typed field returned by a read-only tool or a fixed delegation rule, without a per-task plan or model call. A deterministic sanitizer strips instruction-like regions before the model reads them, and across three backbones no standard templated injection redirected an action to an attacker's target under SPILLWAY.

SPILLWAY admits an action's recipient, account or URL when it appears in the user's request or in a typed field that a read-only tool returned, such as an email's sender.
An address found only in free text, such as an email body, is refused unless the request delegates it.
This check is a set lookup with no model call.
An optional local judge may restore a refused call, never one whose target came from injected text the sanitizer removed.
The repository has recipes for LangChain and LangGraph, the OpenAI Agents SDK, any MCP host and Claude Code hooks.

items.title: ScaleVLA scales vision-language-action models to 552B parameters
items.summary: ScaleVLA connects a 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backbone to a trainable action DiT and compares VLMs from 2B to 552B under a shared training setup. Ten demonstrations outperform a 2B backbone trained with 50 (87.8% vs. 85.6%), LIBERO-PRO success reaches 45.1%, real-world charger insertion improves from 4/10 to 9/10, and median latency per action chunk is 216 ms.

items.title: VoxMel generates speech without an acoustic tokenizer
items.summary: VoxMel is a tokenizer-free autoregressive TTS framework that uses a fixed, exactly invertible two-axis Haar transform to decompose mel spectrograms into Coarse-Mel and residual tiers. Trained on 100K hours of Emilia, the supervised 0.6B model reaches 1.51% WER and 0.738 SIM on test-en and 1.29% CER and 0.755 SIM on test-zh, with GRPO improving these to 1.15% WER / 0.753 SIM and 1.17% CER / 0.776 SIM.

evidence.quote: Papers arxiv:2611.20254 Copy markdown VoxMel TTS Technical Report Published on Nov 15 · Submitted by SII-Guan Wenhao on Nov 17 · VoxDance-Lab Upvote 22 +14 Authors: Wenhao Guan , Jiaxin Ye , Haitao Li , Yifan Duan , Junxi Liu , Wangjin Zhou , Lin Li , Qingyang Hong , Xie Chen Abstract VoxMel is a to

kenizer-free autoregressive TTS framework that uses an invertible two-axis Haar transform to decompose mel spectrograms into Coarse-Mel and residual tiers, enabling stable high-fidelity generation with strong recognition and speaker-similarity results.
In this work, we propose VoxMel, a tokenizer-free framework for autoregressive TTS that makes stable mel modeling tractable through a fixed, exactly invertible two-axis Haar transform .

The transform first decomposes each mel spectrogram along frequency into local averages and a frequency residual , then splits the averaged component along time into Coarse-Mel and a temporal residual .
A language-model backbone with a flow-matching head autoregressively generates Coarse-Mel .
Non-autoregressive residual tiers then predict the temporal residual from Coarse-Mel , followed by the frequency residual conditioned on the reconstructed Frequency-Averaged Mel .
Neither residual is fed back into the autoregressive history .
Trained on 100K hours of Emilia, the supervised 0.6B model obtains 1.51\% WER and 0.738 speaker similarity (SIM) on test-en, and 1.29\% CER and 0.755 SIM on test-zh.
GRPO improves these results to 1.15\% WER / 0.753 SIM and 1.17\% CER / 0.776 SIM, respectively.
We also distill the guided flow head into two- and four-step student s, requiring 2 or 4 head evaluations per coarse frame.
The four-step student retains competitive SIM and nearly matches the supervised model in WER/CER.

View arXiv page View PDF Project page GitHub 92 Add to collection Community guanwenhao Paper submitter about 22 hours ago VoxMel explores a different path for autoregressive TTS: generating directly in the continuous Mel spectrogram space, without relying on learned acoustic tokenizers.
The key idea is to use wavelet decomposition to model acoustic information at different scales.

items.title: MovieRoll rolls out long-form streaming video generation
items.summary: MovieRoll is a base-to-distilled framework that connects streaming fine-tuning, long-rollout distillation, and long-horizon inference, using Window-wise Teacher Forcing (WinTF), hierarchical KV-cache compression (HieraKV), and cumulative long tuning with distribution matching distillation (CuLT-DMD). HieraKV reduces cache memory by up to 78% while improving generation quality, and on HeliosBench MovieRoll-Base stays competitive at 30s while MovieRoll-Distilled scores highest among compared methods up to 60s.

View arXiv page View PDF Project page GitHub 53 Add to collection Community yunyangge Paper submitter about 22 hours ago Streaming video generation must sustain quality beyond the training horizon while handling self-generated history and growing cache costs.
To address these challenges, we present MovieRoll, a base-to-distilled framework that connects streaming fine-tuning, long-rollout distillation, and long-horizon inference.

We first establish a robust multi-step base through Window-wise Teacher Forcing (WinTF), which jointly denoises chunks at progressive noise levels with bidirectional attention within each window and causal access to preceding history.

To retain historical context efficiently, hierarchical KV-cache compression (HieraKV) exploits layer-wise attention patterns, retaining full history in shallow layers and sink--recent history in deeper layers.
This reduces cache memory by up to 78% while improving generation quality.
Building on this base, cumulative long tuning with distribution matching distillation (CuLT-DMD) holds parameters fixed throughout each long self-rollout and averages local gradients before updating.
Each update therefore combines supervision across temporal positions while retaining only one local computation graph, enabling efficient long-rollout training of a few-step generator.

To extend generation beyond the training horizon, KV recomputation bounds context for both models, while guidance annealing (AnnealCFG) reduces guidance toward the clean endpoint to stabilize MovieRoll-Base.
Complementing these modeling advances, FBCA attention and PS-VAE decoding support efficient training and streaming output.

On HeliosBench, MovieRoll-Base remains competitive at 30s after training on videos of up to 15s, and MovieRoll-Distilled achieves the highest total scores among the compared methods across single- and multi-event evaluations up to 60s, combining sustained naturalness with active motion.

items.title: InclusionMed benchmarks medical AI across roles and capabilities
items.summary: InclusionMed is an open medical AI evaluation initiative whose Atlas organizes benchmarks across three healthcare roles and three AI capabilities, with five benchmarks covering three of its nine role-capability cells. Frontier models scored from 17.5 to 49.1 out of 100 on the InclusionMed Index, and the ten highest-ranked models all scored higher on patient communication than on clinical decision-making.

evidence.quote: Papers arxiv:2611.21218 Copy markdown InclusionMed: Benchmarking AI for Inclusive Healthcare Published on Nov 16 · Submitted by Yifan Zhou on Nov 17 #2 Paper of the day Upvote 75 +67 Authors: The InclusionMed Collaboration Abstract InclusionMed is an open medical AI evaluation initiative that audits
and reproduces benchmarks across healthcare roles and capabilities, revealing that model rankings and inference costs vary by context and motivating broader, context-specific evaluation.

Generated by deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Advancing medical AI for inclusive healthcare requires evaluation across diverse healthcare roles, tasks, and care settings, but benchmark coverage remains uneven.
We introduce InclusionMed, an open medical AI evaluation initiative for inclusive healthcare.
The InclusionMed Atlas organizes benchmarks across three healthcare roles and three AI capabilities.
For the first release, we selected four public benchmarks from 388 candidates through structured audits and independent reproduction.
With InclusionMed-DxFiles , our private diagnostic reasoning benchmark , the Atlas contains five benchmarks covering three of its nine role--capability cells.
We evaluated frontier large language models on the Atlas and aggregated their results into the InclusionMed Index , with overall scores ranging from 17.5 to 49.1 out of 100.
The Index also reports scores by healthcare role and AI capability, showing that a model's rank varied with the role or capability considered.
A within-benchmark analysis using task-level tags showed that the ten highest-ranked models in the Index all scored higher on patient communication than on clinical decision-making.
Models with similar Index scores also differed substantially in estimated inference cost .
These findings highlight the need for evaluation covering more diverse healthcare needs and for context-specific model selection.
Through open collaboration and community contributions, InclusionMed seeks to ensure that diverse healthcare needs worldwide shape how medical AI progress is defined and measured.
View arXiv page View PDF Project page GitHub 38 Add to collection Community yingmanji Paper submitter about 21 hours ago InclusionMed is an open evaluation initiative for inclusive healthcare.

Through successive releases of the Atlas and Index, this open collaboration aims to ensure that the diverse healthcare needs of people worldwide guide how progress in medical AI is defined and measured.
The InclusionMed Atlas organizes benchmarks along two axes: healthcare role and AI capability.
The role axis distinguishes patients and the public, healthcare professionals, and healthcare administration professionals; the capability axis distinguishes knowledge, reasoning, and agency.
The Atlas design makes clear which healthcare needs are represented by the included benchmarks and where coverage remains limited.
The InclusionMed Index aggregates model results across the benchmarks included in the Atlas.
In the initial release, each model's Index score is the equally weighted mean of its five benchmark scores.
The Index also reports scores by healthcare role and AI capability, revealing differences in both model rankings and score levels.

items.title: Claude Platform adds linked billing in beta
items.summary: Linked billing lets third-party platforms let end customers pay for Claude API usage without sharing an API key, with usage billed directly to the customer's Claude Platform organization. Customers approve each platform, set monthly spend limits, and can unlink at any time, while platforms can view per-customer request counts, token usage, and models used in Console or via the Usage and Cost Analytics API (beta).

evidence.quote: Linked billing on the Claude Platform Category Product updates Product Claude Platform Date November 17, 2026 Reading time 4 min Share Copy link Contents A more secure alternative to sharing API keys Platforms can offer Claude to customers without building the billing Customers get more visibility a
nd control Getting started Today we're introducing linked billing on the Claude Platform in beta.
Third-party platforms, such as coding agents and workflow automation tools, can let their end customers pay for Claude API usage without sharing an API key.
End customers keep their existing Anthropic billing and set their own spend limits, and platforms get a simpler, more secure way to offer Claude.

A more secure alternative to sharing API keys Paying for Claude API usage on a third-party platform usually means sharing an API key, which works like a password: anyone who has the key can make requests billed to the customer, so the platform has to keep it safe.
With linked billing, customers link their Claude Platform organization instead, and usage is billed directly to it.
No API key changes hands, so platforms have no customer keys to store, encrypt or rotate, and customers’ API keys never leave their organization.
Platforms can see usage for each linked customer.
Customers approve each linked platform, set a spend limit, and can unlink at any time.
Linked billing on the Claude Platform Platforms can offer Claude to customers without building the billing Linked billing gives platforms a new way to offer Claude to their customers.
Platforms send requests, and Anthropic bills the end customers directly.
With linked billing, platforms can: Launch faster.
Anthropic hosts the approval flow and the billing, so there’s no metering or invoicing to build.
Understand usage by customer.
Get each linked customer’s request count, token usage and models used in Console, or programmatically with the Usage and Cost Analytics API (beta).
Choose who pays.
Decide on each request whether the platform or the end customer pays, so platforms can pass Claude API costs to customers or cover some features themselves by product or instance.
Customers get more visibility and control Customers can easily link to platforms using Anthropic’s hosted flow.
They can then draw down from their existing Anthropic commitment, or pay as they go.
With linked billing, customers can also: Link once for the whole organization.
A Console user with an Owner, Admin, or Billing role approves the link, so it works the same for individual developers and large teams.
Set limits for each platform.
Customers can set a monthly spend limit for each platform, or a default that applies to each one.
See where API spend goes.
Console shows spend for each linked platform.
Unlink at any time.
Customers can unlink directly from Console.
Requests run in the platform’s organization, so settings in the customer’s organization, such as IP allowlists, encryption keys, and data retention, don’t apply.

Platforms that support linked billing today include Asana, ClickHouse, Factory, Gumloop, Harness, Higgsfield AI, Kilo Code, Linear, Major, Mintlify, Omni, OpenArt, Niteshift, Railway, Ramp, Runlayer, Tessera, Tines, and Warp.
Getting started Linked billing is available today in beta on the Claude Platform.
Third-party platforms can add support by creating an app in Console and following the steps in the docs .

items.title: PaperOrchestra automates research paper writing with agents
items.summary: PaperOrchestra is a multi-agent framework from Google Cloud AI Research that turns ideas and experimental logs into submission-ready LaTeX manuscripts, covering outline generation, literature review, section writing, content refinement, and plotting. It also produces generated visuals such as plots and conceptual diagrams, adheres to target conference templates, and ships an interactive Streamlit demo.

evidence.quote: s 🎻 PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing
Yiwen Song 1 , Yale Song 1 , Tomas Pfister 1 , and Jinsung Yoon 1
1 Google Cloud AI Research
PaperOrchestra is a multi-agent framework for automated AI research paper writing.

It flexibly transforms unconstrained pre-writing materials (ideas and experimental logs) into submission-ready LaTeX manuscripts, including comprehensive literature synthesis and generated visuals, such as plots and conceptual diagrams.

Acting like an orchestrated team of specialized agents, it handles outline generation, literature review, section writing, content refinement, and plotting to close the gap between raw research materials and submission ready papers.
Multi-Agent Pipeline : Orchestrates specialized agents (Outline, Literature Review, Section Writing, Content Refinement, Plotting) for end-to-end paper generation.
Comprehensive Literature Synthesis : Automatically searches, prioritizes, and integrates relevant literature into the manuscript.
Visuals Generation : Generates plots and supports the inclusion of conceptual diagrams.
LaTeX Automation : Produces submission-ready LaTeX manuscripts adhering to target conference templates.
Environment Setup : The project relies on a Conda environment named paper_orchestra .
You can set up a similar environment with Python 3.11 and install the required dependencies.
Interactive Demo
We provide an interactive Streamlit demo for the paper generation pipeline.
For instructions on how to run and use it, please refer to the README.md in the frontend directory.
Project Structure
autoraters/ : Contains scripts for automated evaluation.
methods/ : Core logic for agents and pipeline execution.
templates/ : LaTeX templates for target conferences, you can add your own template by creating a new subfolder under this directory.
utils/ : Utility functions for API calls, PDF handling, etc.
This is not an officially supported Google product.
